summary: ```markdown # End-To-End Clo Virtual Series | Webinar 01: Custom Asset Library - Create & Manage ## Introduction Hello everyone, welcome to the End-To-End Clo Virtual Series. I'm Raj, a Design and Implementation Specialist at the Clo India office. And I am Uttra, also a Design Implementation Specialist at the Clo India office. We are super excited to launch this bi-monthly series focused on updating your workflow. In each session, we'll show you how to use your tools smarter, highlight the latest features, and share practical tips to help you boost your efficiency, support your growth, and, of course, get the best return on your investment. Right now, it's all about making your workflow smoother and getting the most value from the tools you already know. ## Webinar Series Overview This is basically an overview of the lineup of our webinar series that we have planned. ### Session Lineup 1. **Digital Asset Library**: Today’s focus is on learning how to create different assets and store them in your library, manage them, and effectively use them for later stages. 2. **Design Proto**: Use the assets you've just created to make quick ideations and review them in closet. 3. **Fit Proto**: Refine those same styles and make them fit-ready, performing proper construction. 4. **Production Ready**: Use these assets to make them production-ready for your plotter, look at your consumption, and generate tech packs. 5. **Marketing and E-commerce**: Use the renders and images from your creations for marketing on various platforms. ## Digital Asset Library Let's go ahead and talk about the first webinar, which is about the Digital Asset Library: how you can create it and manage it. ### What is a Digital Asset Library? A Digital Asset Library is a centralized repository designed to store, manage, and organize digital assets. ### Definition of Digital Assets In terms of CLO, digital assets include: - CLO avatars - Fabrics - Textures - Patterns (DXF, rule files) - Hardware and trims - Color palettes Having all of these repositories of data will streamline your workflow and help you make faster decisions and design iterations. ### File Extensions Here are some file extensions you should know: - **Avatars**: AVT, AVS, OBJ - **Fabrics**: Z, ZFAB - **Textures**: PNG, JPEG, GRP - **Patterns**: DXF, rule files - **Hardware and Trims**: TRM, SST, PPT, BTN - **Color Palettes**: CCCO, ANDAC ### Benefits of a Digital Asset Library Some benefits include: - Centralization of data - Increased collaboration - Increased efficiency - Consistent brand image A quote to remember: "The future of creativity isn't in making more content. It's in mastering the art of finding, reusing, and amplifying what you already have." ### Who Can Use a Digital Asset Library? - Pattern makers: Create pattern blocks and store them for future use. - Designers: Use assets to create quick design variations. - 3D Team: Store and reuse assets. - Merchandisers: Link assets with component-based design. - Product Managers, Buyers, QA Team, Sourcing Team: All can benefit from a Digital Asset Library. A quote to reflect on: "A digital asset library doesn't just store content; it builds bridges between teams, turning scattered files into shared success." ## Creating a Digital Asset Library You can create all of these initial assets on CLO, where the creation of any 3D happens, and then upload them on CLOet to manage them. CLO and CLOet are seamlessly connected, allowing you to transfer data between them. ### Creating Assets in CLO We'll talk about how to create different kinds of avatars, fabrics, textures, patterns, and trims on CLO. Please note that all workflows and features discussed are based on CLO version 2025.0. #### Creating Avatars You can either use the default library of avatars or customize avatars based on your specifications using the Avatar Editor. The Auto Convert to Avatar feature allows you to convert any body scan OBJ or 3D OBJ into a CLO compatible avatar. - **Default Avatars**: Access the avatar tab in the library to see various avatars. - **Customization**: Use the accessory folder to customize hair, shoes, and poses. - **Measurement Tools**: Use circumference and surface tapes to get accurate measurements. #### Saving Avatars Once you have customized your avatar, you can save it in CLO format. Important: the file format for CLO avatars is `.abasa`. ### Avatar Editor The Avatar Editor allows for detailed customization based on specific measurements. Use it to adjust width, height, cup size, and adjust the shape of the avatar. #### Key Features of the Avatar Editor: - **Measurement Adjustment**: Change measurements and see real-time updates. - **Shape Customization**: Adjust hand, head, hips, and bust shape. - **Save Custom Sizes**: Save your custom avatar sizes with the appropriate file format. ### Auto Convert to Avatar The Auto Convert feature allows you to convert any OBJ into a CLO compatible avatar. Select the OBJ file and choose the conversion option that meets your needs. ## Patterns Moving on to patterns, if you are using a 2D CAD software, you can import DXF and rule files into CLO. You can also draft patterns from scratch using the CLO pattern drafter or the AI pattern drafter. ### Drafting Patterns in CLO - **Drafting from Scratch**: Use guidelines and measurement tools to draft patterns. - **AI Pattern Drafter**: This feature allows you to draft patterns based on images or specifications. ### Importing Patterns When importing patterns, ensure that the DXF and rule files have the same name and are located in the same folder. ### Exporting Patterns Once patterns are drafted, you can export them as DXF files for use in other software. ## Fabrics In CLO, you can utilize fabric presets or create custom fabric libraries from scratch. ### Understanding Fabrics Fabrics can be divided into two parts: 1. **Physical Properties**: Weight, stiffness, stretch. 2. **Visual Properties**: Color, texture, print, and reflection. ### Creating Custom Fabrics You can create custom fabrics using the CLO fabric digitization service or the CLO ZFAB kit. You can also use the CLO AI fabric creator to define fabric properties. ### Visualizing Fabrics Visual properties can be adjusted using the AI texture generator or by importing texture images for seamless patterns. ## Trims and Custom Assets CLO also allows for the creation and management of trims, including buttons, zippers, and top stitches. ### Creating Custom Trims - **Buttons**: Use the button library to create custom buttons. - **Top Stitches**: Create different stitch types and customize them using images or 3D models. ### Saving and Organizing Assets All custom assets should be saved with clear and consistent nomenclature for easy access and reusability. ## Managing Your Digital Asset Library ### CLOet and Workflow Management CLOet is a cloud-based platform for managing assets and facilitating collaboration among teams. ### Creating a Group in CLOet When creating a group, ensure that all team members can access a centralized library to improve workflow efficiency. ### Best Practices for Asset Management - Maintain a centralized database for easier collaboration. - Categorize assets by brand or type for easier access. - Ensure all files are properly named and organized. ## Conclusion Thank you for joining this session of the End-To-End Clo Virtual Series. We hope you found the information useful and that you are excited to implement these tools to enhance your workflow and efficiency. ```

summary: ```markdown # Fur Generation | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name's Phoebe, and I'm going to show you this really cool new feature called Fur Strand. It's going to allow you to see all of your fur in your 3D window. So, let's have some fun while we learn and dive on in! ## Locating the Fur Strand Feature Okay, so here I have my 3D window. What we're first going to go through is where this feature is, how this feature works, things to know about it, and then we're going to go through a workflow on how you could apply it into your everyday life. ### Where is This Feature? Well, it's where all of our material types are. If I go to my object browser up top here on my right, I can select my fabric. Now, as you all probably know already, when you select a fabric, there will be a yellow highlight in your 3D window telling you which piece is applied to that fabric or has that fabric applied to it. Here I have Fabric 2. It's applied to this piece. I can then go down into my Property Editor, which is right below the object browser. If I scroll down a bit underneath materials, I'll see "Type." This type is telling me what type of fabric this is. This is our Fur Render Only fabric. ### Activating Fur Strand Now, if I go to this dropdown, I can see right above Fur Render Only, there's Fur Strand. Fur Strand is what's going to allow you to see this in your 3D window. So I'm going to select this, and it's visible now. Now I can see it here in my 3D window. Looks amazing! ## Viewing Options for Fur Strand ### Control Options Some things to know: you can control how this is viewed. There are three options on how this is viewed. We're going to get to where you can view that in a minute. Also, what to know is when you switch from Fur Render to Fur Strand, it does reset all of your properties. You will have to reapply them all. You can even see here for preset now is default. Originally, when it was Fur Render, it was Fox. So now it's at default. I can just easily go to Fox, and it will show me my Fox Fur. ### System Compatibility Also, to know, this currently works in Windows. We do not have it in MacOS. Apologies, but for all you Windows users, it's great! Additionally, this does work in your render window. You do not have to switch to Fur Render to see this in render; you can keep it all in as Fur Strand, and you can see it all. ## User Settings for Fur Strand Let's go into our user settings to see all of the different ways in which you can view your fur in your 3D window. ### Accessing User Settings Here at the very top toolbar, I can go to Settings, and from Settings, I can go to User Settings. Here, I'll select User Settings and go into my 3D section. Right below my 3D section is Fur Strand Shape. So, our default is always "Plane" because that helps the software run quickly and also provides a good amount of information for your fur. ### Viewing Modes You can also use "Line" or "Cylinder." #### Plane To help you out, in what you're seeing in Plane, let's hit close and zoom in a bit. For Plane, what you can see is kind of like the width of that fur because you can see the width, but you can't see the height or the depth or thickness of it. You can see how long it will be, but it looks flat. #### Line If I go to User Settings and then choose Line, I'm going to hit close. Line will not give you much information on thickness or width, but it will tell you how long it is, as it will be a straight line. This is helpful for quick edits. #### Cylinder Next, we're going to User Settings and then into 3D and select Cylinder. Cylinder will give you the most amount of information because it will display every single strand as a cylinder. You can see how thick it is, how wide it is, and how long it is. However, this does slow down your window a bit, so if you're going to do a lot of edits, it might get frustrating quickly. ## Comparing Fur Strand and Fur Render Now, let's dive into rendering and compare the differences between Fur Strand and Fur Render Only. ### Rendering Differences There is a bit of a difference between the two when you render them. Fur Strand is much closer to real life than Fur Render. It's a big improvement, as it shows how the fur falls and how light interacts with it, making it feel more realistic. In contrast, Fur Render gives a classic representation of fur but may not account for how it drapes as much. ## Workflow Ideas Now let's discuss some workflow ideas. Here is my garment, and this is probably how you all are going to work soon because everything you have is rendered, right? ### Workflow Steps - Everything is Fur Render Only. If you switch to Strand, all information gets changed. - Use Control + Z to undo changes. - Copy from Fur Strand and then go to Fur Render, paste, and apply changes. ### Saving and Applying Fabrics You might need to go through this process for all of them. I can see that my color stayed, which is really helpful. If you didn't save it initially, you can go back and select the fabric and hit apply. ### Finalizing the Workflow Once you have everything set up, you can hit Interactive and see everything together. The coloring will be nice, and you can review how it all looks. ## Conclusion Thank you all so much for watching! I hope you enjoyed the video. If you have any questions, use that comment section down below. A Clo 3D designer will get back to you. Keep having fun in CLO, and thanks again for watching! ```

summary: ```markdown # USD Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone! I have some great updates to share with you about the USD file format. Let’s jump in and have some fun while we learn. ## What is USD File Format? For those of you who might be wondering, "Phoebe, what is the USD file format?" I recommend skipping this video if you're unfamiliar with it. The USD file format is primarily used in the entertainment and gaming industries. It’s essential when connecting to major 3D engines and studios, such as Unreal or Omniverse, among others. Our goal is to make it easier for you to create digital art that extends beyond production into the digital realm. If you're not ready for that yet, don't worry; you might be one day! ## New Features in USD File Format We have made several improvements to our USD file format! ### Accessing the USD Layering Option Where can you find these updates? First, go to the settings menu. Open the new USD layering option by navigating to **Settings** > **Display** > **Window** > **USD Layer**. - Once you open that up, you will see the USD layer option on the left. - You can create multiple layers, export them, or even clear everything and start fresh. This is an exciting update—USD layering is now possible in Clo! ### Exporting USD Files We’ve also made updates to the exporting process for USD files. When you go to **File** > **Export** > **USD**, your UV editor will pop up. - If you uncheck the box, it won't matter, but I recommend checking it so you can see all your textures in the USD format. - You now have the ability to rename your meshes and materials, allowing for better organization of your work. ### Garment Simulation Data Additionally, you can include garment simulation information along with fur strand data during the export. Please note that I currently don’t have any fur in my project, so I won’t be checking that option. - Another great feature is the option to specify your up-axis; I set mine to Y. - Once you hit okay, the software will bake and create the entire texture for you. ### Importing USD Files After exporting, you can import your USD file. For example, if I go to **Import** > **Add** > **USD** and select my file, I can see the USD layering automatically pop up. - The dropdown menu allows you to view all of your meshes. - When you select a mesh, you can access all the pattern information and simulation data for the fabrics. ## Conclusion There’s a lot of information to digest here, especially if you’re new to the 3D pipeline or the After CL environment. It can be overwhelming at first, but these updates are truly exciting. Feel free to select your patterns and adjust settings as needed. This will significantly enhance your workflow if you plan to integrate with other software like Unreal or Omniverse. ## Final Thoughts I hope you enjoyed the video! If you have any questions, please use the comment section below, and someone will get back to you. Don’t forget to like and subscribe to our channel for more great videos. Thanks again for watching, and keep having fun in Clo! ```

summary: ```markdown # Group Internal Lines | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I have a great update for you with internal lines in our 2025.0 release. So, let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Grouping Internal Lines Now, what you can do with internal lines is, get ready for it, group them! Using your Transform Pattern tool at the top here, you can select all of your internal lines or shapes. These are all shapes, and these were traced from a graphic. ### Grouping Process 1. Right-click on top of the selected lines or shapes. 2. Choose the **Group** option. 3. Now, when you move this group, they will all move together. If you scale this, they will all scale together. ### Editing Patterns Individually If you go to your Edit Pattern tool, however, it will then start to adjust individually, as you can see. You can also select some lines individually. All of that can then be right-clicked and grouped or ungrouped. ### Ungrouping and Reselecting You can select all of these shapes, right-click, and choose **Ungroup**. Then, you could reselect them all and right-click to group them together again—all with your Edit Pattern tool. Just know that the grouping will be honored when using your Transform Pattern tool. The Transform Pattern tool will respect the grouping the most. ## Working with Lines Now, let’s talk about lines specifically. I'm going to go down here and go to my Transform Pattern tool again. If I just go to my Edit Pattern tool and try to select these internal lines, you will notice that the group option will not be available. ### Selecting Internal Lines To select these internal lines, hold down **Shift** and click once with your left mouse button to select each line. After selecting all desired lines, right-click on top of the selection and choose **Group**. ### Moving and Resizing Groups Now these lines will be grouped together. If you click and move them, it’s pretty cool, right? You can right-click and delete if needed. If you want to resize all of the selected lines, you can do so while they are grouped. You can also right-click to group or ungroup them. But remember, with your Edit Pattern tool, it will only edit the individual lines. With your Transform Pattern tool, it will follow and honor the grouping. ## Conclusion Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe. Thanks again so much for watching. Keep having fun and glow! ```

The background is new and cool, but our faces have also received some nice updates as well. ### Face Generation First off, you can do a prompt or an image. If you have an image, you can just hit upload. Here, I have my image and I can hit generate. **Tip:** The best images are front-facing with clean lighting—very easy to understand and see. There should be nothing blocking the face. ### Output Image Refinement Now, we do have some updates for our output image. You can always have refinement options for hair, hands, or garment. - If I want to refine the hair, I can select "hair," and it will refine it for a bit. - If I also want some refinement in the hands, I could select "hands." - If I want to refine the garment, I can always select this option, which will refine the garment a bit. Everything looks great—I've got a really nice outfit here, and the hands, hair, and face look amazing! ## Background Generation Now, let's go into my background. Here are some checks I want to remind you all about: 1. It’s always great to bring in a just-rendered image. It’s best if you render it, hit play, and then go to the magic wand. 2. You don’t always have to do that, but it often gives you the best results. 3. Make sure your face is all set, and you like your avatar and garment before going to the background, as this is the best workflow to achieve optimal results. ### Using Prompts for Backgrounds Once everything is set, you can just go to the background. Here's my target image. Now, let's go to the text prompt option. I can type something in. For example, I want a "back startup studio" kind of theme with a "mystical" vibe. There’s a pin icon to help maintain the current prompt to generate similar results, along with random prompt options. Let’s see what else we've got. If I’m not happy with my previous prompt, I can delete it and hit generate again. ## Saving Your Work If I’m happy with what I just created, which I am, I can hit save. You can also use the history option to see all of your previous renders. summary: ```markdown # Keyframe Animation Editor ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I have some great updates to share with you for our animation. We've updated quite a lot in our 2025.0 release. So, let's dive in and have some fun while we learn! ## Animation Editor Overview Okay, so here I have my screen. There’s a lot for me to share with you, so we're going to try to break this up into as many parts as possible so it's easy for you to follow. Let's first just start with a simple overview of where everything is. ### Changes to the Animation Editor Our animation editor has changed. It's no longer in mode. We can go to the very top toolbar and select "Animation." Once you select "Animation," you can then click on "Animation Editor." Instead of adjusting the entire screen, this animation editor will pop up at the very bottom. You can hover over the editor; your cursor will change, allowing you to move this up or down for easier viewing. Within this editor, you'll see controls for recording, rewinding, going back, playing, and navigating through frames. ### Key Features The key features available include: - **Record, Rewind, Play**: Basic controls for animation playback. - **Go to Previous/Next Frame**: Navigate through your animation. - **Speed Controls**: Options for 1x, 0.5x, 0.25x, 2x, 4x, and 8x playback speed. - **Auto Key Framing**: A new feature for simplifying animation. - **Camera Key Framing**: A refresher on camera key framing, including viewfinder controls and the option to hide camera paths. - **Simulation Quality**: Choose between stable or custom settings. - **Configurations**: Play type, frame stepping, current frame, scene time warp, display units, and frames per second (FPS). If you are not a video editing expert, focus mainly on: - Recording and playing - Key frames and camera settings - Adjusting simulation quality when necessary ### Play Region Control You can control your play region from the top of the animation editor. Hover over the edge, click, and hold down to adjust your play region. You can expand or contract the view by using the bar below. ## Animation Layers All animation layers will be shown here. If you're recording, you'll see the new layers appear. You can select, delete, or manage these layers as needed. The layering system allows you to manage all the animations you're working on effectively. ### Adding Animation There are several ways to add animation: 1. **Add Animation Button**: Click to add directly. 2. **Recording**: Record your motion to create animations. 3. **Library Drag-and-Drop**: Use your library of motions by dragging and dropping or double-clicking to add animations. 4. **Property Editor**: Use the property editor to insert key frames, which adds animation. ## Managing Animation Layers You can manage your animation layers in various ways: - **Hide/Show Layers**: Use the eye icon to hide layers. - **Cut/Merge Layers**: Right-click to cut or merge selected layers. - **Key Frame Management**: Every diamond you see represents a key frame. You can select multiple key frames to delete or adjust as necessary. ## Adding Animation: Simulation Properties ### Gravity and Air Damping When you add simulation properties, you’ll need to switch to custom for simulation quality. You can play around with gravity settings and air damping. For example, you can set gravity to zero and see how the motion changes. ### Demonstration of Simulation You can record the effects of gravity in your animation. As you adjust gravity settings, you can see how the object behaves when influenced by gravity or when it is removed. ## Wind Controller The wind controller allows you to activate and adjust wind effects in your animation. Using auto key framing for wind adjustments can simplify the process of creating dynamic movements. ### Transform Options For transform options, you can set key frames to constant, linear, or cubic. Each affects how the object moves between key frames. ## Adding Animation: Pins and Camera ### Using Pins Before you can animate pins, you must add them to your 3D window. Each pin can be activated or deactivated, and you can add key frames for their movements. ### Camera Animation You can add camera animations with various options, such as moving and rotating the camera. This allows you to create dynamic visual presentations of your animations. ## Avatar Animation The avatar system allows for detailed joint manipulation. You can turn on auto key framing, adjust joints, and create smooth transitions in movements. ### Pattern and Fabric Changes You can change fabric patterns dynamically within your animation. Adjust the properties and see how different fabrics react in real-time. ## Color Way Adjustments Color ways can be animated similarly to patterns, allowing you to switch between different color schemes throughout the animation. ## Creating an Animation Together Let’s summarize how to create a simple animation. Start by adding simulation properties and adjusting gravity. Next, incorporate wind effects and camera movements. Finally, add your avatar and adjust the color way to complete the animation. ### Recording and Finalizing After setting everything up, hit record to see how it all looks. Remember, it’s okay to make adjustments as needed to refine your animation. ## Conclusion Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section below. Don't forget to like and subscribe! Check out all of our great videos on our YouTube channel, and keep having fun with Glow. ```

For example, they can directly modify the visual board there to make it more customized, allowing the vendor to understand your final direction. ## Co-Creation and Material Presentation This vendor can also base their 3D designs on the updated direction and present more materials in the virtual showroom on CLO-SET. Once the direction is confirmed, if you like the design proposed by your vendors, you can comment on and modify the outline, including small details in their files. Alternatively, you can let your vendors create or modify it for you. You can work with your vendors who will provide you with the pattern blocks, trims, and fabrics in digital format. When the materials are ready, designers can overcome challenges and not limit their creativity due to a lack of available materials. ## Importance of Transparency with Vendors On the brand side, it is crucial that we are super transparent with our vendors. It's not only about the 3D quality or which workflows or types of files we need to protect the quality of the 3D garment, but more importantly, to communicate the vision so they understand our roadmap. This understanding is vital as their role involves a lot of investment. ## Vendor Investment and Asset Reusability It is an investment in the right equipment, software, and talent, which is difficult to find and nurture. You don’t need to wait to have the physical sample in order to do promotions. Vendors can also reuse the assets and consolidate the files they created to present their capabilities and find more business opportunities. For example, they can create an e-lookbook and conduct outbound sales. You can use these 3D files for your e-commerce website and predict how consumers will like your products. The more brands communicate their commitment and vision, the easier it becomes for vendors to join the journey with us and make the necessary investments.

summary: ```markdown # Linking Patterns & Symmetry | Clo Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey all you clovers, it's Phoebe here. Today, we're going to talk all about linking and unlinking and where it can be applied, such as pattern outlines, internal lines, and more. So let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn. ## Overview of Linking Options On my screen, you can see there are four different options: symmetry, instance and layer clones, linking to pattern outline, and the linking tool. These are the four core ways in which you can link things within Clo, meaning that when one thing happens to something, it affects another thing. ### Where to Find Linking Options Most of these options are found in your Transform Pattern Tool. You can access a lot of these by right-clicking within the Transform Pattern Tool. #### Symmetry To achieve symmetry, select your pattern using the Transform Pattern Tool, right-click, and you'll see various symmetric options including half symmetry. You can also achieve symmetry options with your Edit Pattern Tool. For instance, if I select a line and right-click, I can see some symmetric options for unfolding. #### Instance Patterns For instance patterns, which are exact copies of a pattern, select your pattern piece, right-click, and find the instance pattern option. #### Layer Clones You can also select a pattern, right-click, and see options for layering clones. This is great because when you layer clone, they are linked together, meaning what happens to one will happen to another. ### Linking to Pattern Outline Also still within the Transform Pattern Tool, you can select an internal line, right-click, and choose "Link to Pattern Outline." This will link your internal line to a pattern outline, which is very useful. ## Using the Edit Pattern Tool Moving away from the Transform Pattern Tool, we can go to the Edit Pattern Tool. Here, you can select a line, right-click, and find the "Link Line" option. This option can also be found when you are sewing things. By going to your Edit Sewing Tool, you can select certain sewing lines, right-click, and hit "Link Line." ## Understanding Symmetry Now that we know where everything is and how to access it, let's discuss what each option does. ### Half Symmetry Half symmetry is applied to one pattern piece and allows you to divide that pattern equally in half, where one side is the symmetric duplicate of the other. If I go to my Edit Pattern Tool and move a point, it will mirror the movement. You can achieve this through right-clicking and selecting "Half Symmetric Pattern" in the Transform Pattern Tool. ### Creating Symmetric Patterns You can unfold with symmetric editing and sewing, allowing for a symmetric line to be created. However, if you simply unfold the pattern outline, it will not create a symmetric line. To create a true symmetric half, use "Half Symmetric Pattern" in the Transform Pattern Tool. ## Instance Patterns and Layer Clones An instance pattern is an exact copy of the selected pattern. When you select a point in an instance pattern, it selects the exact same point, unlike symmetry which mirrors the point. Layer cloning creates an exact copy of your pattern and automatically sews it for you, placing it directly underneath or above the pattern. If you edit one, the other will edit as well. ## Linking Internal Lines Linking to a pattern outline is done using the Transform Pattern Tool. Select your internal line, right-click, and choose "Link to Pattern Outline." You'll see a prompt indicating to click on a start and end point to select a line. You can also create links using the linking tool. With your Edit Pattern Tool, you can select a line, right-click, and say "Link Lines." This will provide guidance on how the lines will move together. ## Practical Application: Simple Workflow Here, I have a relatively simple garment. I will demonstrate a fundamental workflow where linking patterns improves efficiency. 1. **Create Symmetric Copies**: Select the patterns, right-click, and create a symmetric pattern with sewing. 2. **Unfold Symmetric Editing**: Select all relevant lines using the Edit Pattern Tool, right-click, and unfold symmetric editing with sewing. ### Benefits of Symmetry With symmetric patterns, adjustments in the 3D window work better because you only arrange half of your pattern. You only need to sew half the pattern, improving efficiency significantly. ## Intermediate Workflow Now, let's tackle a more complex garment. I already have simple symmetry applied. 1. **Apply Half Symmetry**: Right-click on the collar and apply half symmetry. 2. **Layer Cloning**: Use the layer clone option to create additional plackets without duplicating work. ### Linking Internal Lines Ensure that the internal lines and pattern outlines of the pocket are linked. You can sew the patterns and then link the lines to create cohesive adjustments. ## Advanced Workflow In this section, we have a garment with no symmetry applied. 1. **Create Half Symmetry**: Select the skirt, right-click, and apply half symmetry. 2. **Link Editing with Sewing**: After creating internal lines, link them to the pattern outline. ### Final Adjustments Select multiple lines and link them together. Remember to unlink when necessary to avoid clutter and confusion in your design. ## Conclusion Thank you for watching! I hope you found this information useful. Remember to utilize the core linking features such as symmetry in your projects. As you grow more comfortable, start using the linking line tools and the linking to pattern outline features to work faster, smarter, and more efficiently. Don’t forget to subscribe and like if you enjoyed this video, and check out other great videos on our channel. If you have any questions, feel free to leave them in the comments below. ```

summary: # Kaneda's Outfit by Sam Zona ## Introduction Last week, we used the virtual sewing machine to create one half of one of the best outfits in anime. Today, we're tackling part two: Kaneda's iconic biker jacket. Luckily, I already drafted a biker jacket pattern in a past video, which serves as a great lesson in virtual pattern making. You can always work off of an existing pattern to save you tons of time. ## Pattern Modification I went ahead and got rid of all those buttons and zippers to start clean and changed the fabric to match Kaneda's pants that I made a few weeks ago. According to my references, this jacket has features of a biker jacket but also the oversized fit of a bomber jacket. ### Waistband Addition The waistband was the first addition I made, and I sewed it into place. After that, I moved on to the shoulder pad-like additions, which is a pretty unique feature that I haven't seen on any real-life references. I made sure to use the fill tool as well to really puff them up and give them a protective padding type of look. Watching these shoulder pads basically inflate with the filling was super satisfying to simulate. ## Pocket Flaps and Button Details Next, I drew out some pocket flaps and sewed those down to the front, further meshing the biker and bomber jacket looks together. I placed silver buttons along an internal line with their respective buttonholes on the front placket. I threaded the buttons through and added one for the collar as well. These buttons are pretty different from the square clasp fasteners shown in the anime, but I just couldn't find anything similar. ## Final Adjustments Then, I elasticized the waistband for a better fit, and I think it's really starting to come together. Just enough for me to add my own little twist on things. I figured the jacket could be a bit more padded, so I added rounded elbow pads, which perfectly achieved that look for me. It looks very epic and also badass from the back view, if you ask me. ## Iconic Back Detail Now, there's just one final touch to add to the back of this jacket: the iconic blue and yellow pill capsule that serves as a symbol for the entire theme of societal control and rebellion in the film. I drew this using internal lines, cut the shape out as its own pattern piece, and sewed it down to the back to be featured as an applique graphic. ## Conclusion That's the finished jacket! I'm pretty satisfied with how it came out, but leave a comment letting me know if you liked my iteration of it. Here's a look at the full outfit. I will see you guys in the next one. Bye! [Music]

After unzipping the folder, simply drag and drop it into Clo to start using it. The downloaded zip file contains two key files: a shoe outsole trim file and a project file with an outsole avatar and pre-drawn 3D pen lines. Then right-click on an empty area in the window and select Mirror Paste. You'll now see a mirrored copy of the upper aligned with the outsole. ## Attaching the Outsole At this stage, the outsole and upper patterns are not yet attached. If you register the shoe in this state, the trim outsole will not be included in the accessory file. You'll use the Glue function to attach the outsole trim to the upper patterns. Glue allows trims to be bonded to garment patterns, and it's essential to use this function to ensure that the outsole is registered as part of the final shoe accessory. To make this easier, press the number zero on your keyboard to switch to the bottom view. Then click once on the outsole in the 3D window. Since the dummy creation process is the same as in previous tutorials, we'll go through this part quickly. If you need a detailed explanation, please refer to the tutorial link in the video description. We recommend starting this video from the point where the saved dummy file is imported. After importing the dummy pattern, adjust its position. Then delete the insole pattern from the dummy and sew it to the insole pattern of the upper. ### Setting Collision Values Next, select all dummy patterns. Set the collision value to 15 and apply strengthen. Because the outsole trim may affect the simulation, we'll also deactivate it. To do this, right-click on the outsole trim and select Deactivate from the menu. Then freeze the upper patterns to keep their shape. Now simulate the dummy. You'll see that the simulation runs smoothly without interference from the outsole. If any part of the upper is sticking out, adjust its position so it stays within the dummy during simulation. Once the dummy fully wraps the sneakers, it should be invisible. To do this, select the fabric applied to the dummy and set its opacity value to zero. ## Finalizing the Sneaker Design This completes the entire shoe-making process in Clo. Now save your project file. Let's align the sneaker with the Clo avatar so we can check the fit and appearance before registering it as an accessory. First, clear the current workspace to start with a clean scene. Then open the Clo female avatar. Since we're working with sneakers, we'll need to set the avatar to a heel-down position. To do that, delete the default heel shoes the avatar is currently wearing. Next, import the saved sneaker project. At this point, you'll notice that the sneaker and avatar positions do not match. We'll adjust the alignment during the accessory registration process in the next step. ## Registering the Shoe as an Accessory Now that we've attached the outsole to the upper, let's finalize the process by registering the finished shoe as a Clo accessory file. The registration method is the same as in the shoe last tutorial, so feel free to refer to that video if you need a detailed walkthrough. First, select all the sneaker patterns. Then right-click on the selected patterns in the 3D window, go to Convert, and click to Avatar Accessory. In the Register Accessory window, set the accessory type to Shoes and Flats. Under Object, select Patterns and make sure that no pattern pieces are missing. ### Adjusting the Shoe Position Next, use the gizmo to adjust the position of the shoe so that it aligns properly with the avatar's foot. To automatically create the opposite side, check the option Mirror Creation. This will generate a mirrored copy of the shoe on the other foot. Once the alignment looks good, click Save to complete the process and register the shoe as a Clo accessory file. ## Applying the Registered Accessory Finally, let's load the registered accessory and apply it to the Clo avatar. From the Clo library, open the MIA avatar. Then load the Dozacs file you saved earlier. title: Everywear To Tiktok Ar Tutorial (English/한국어)
description: Learn how to convert garments from CLO into TikTok Effect House AR Filter using EveryWear! LOTS of links in Description!
transcript:
Tutorial_EveryWear_Tiktok AR (EN)
01. Introduction & Purpose
Hello, everyone!
Have you ever wanted to create your very own AR filter on TikTok featuring a unique outfit?
Imagine wearing the outfit you designed and turning it into a one-of-a-kind filter!
With EveryWear, the process is much easier and more fun than you might think.
To explain it simply, we all know TikTok, right? 
It's the go-to platform for creating, sharing, and enjoying short-form videos!
In this tutorial, we'll walk through the process of transforming garments created in CLO or Marvelous Designer into a TikTok AR filter using EveryWear, Photoshop, and Effect House.
If you re new to EveryWear,
we recommend checking out the basic tutorials first to get familiar with the fundamentals.
We've included useful reference links in the description be sure to take a look! 
Now, let s get started!
02. Effect House Guidelines
To create a TikTok AR filter, 
we need to use Effect House, TikTok's official AR development program.  
First, download and install the program from the link below.
This tutorial is based on Effect House version 4.11.2.
We've also prepared a manual and important guidelines
for creating your own AR filters
be sure to check the description for details!
When creating your filter in Effect House,
make sure to follow these technical requirements.
We've also provided a Template Body Mesh file for Effect House,
which is essential for designing outfits. 
You can find the download link in the description, so make sure to grab it!
By following these guidelines, 
you'll be able to create a more stable and stunning AR filter. 
Now, let's move on to the next step!
03. EveryWear
First, we will create and dress the avatar using CLO.
Then, we'll use EveryWear for garment optimization, rigging and bake map creation.
Since EveryWear works the same in both CLO and Marvelous Designer, 
feel free to use the software you're most comfortable with.
Downloading the Outfit & Importing the Avatar
The outfit used in this tutorial is provided by CONNECT. 
Click the link in the card above to access CONNECT.
Add the garment to your cart,
complete the purchase, and download the file.
Import the downloaded file into CLO or Marvelous Designer to begin working.
Next, you'll also need to import the BodyRigTemplate.fbx file for Effect House.
Simply drag and drop the file into your workspace.
When importing, 
make sure to match the settings shown in the provided reference image.
Fitting
Currently, both the avatar and the outfit are positioned below 
the Ground.
To correct this, we first need to disable the Ground Collision setting.
Right-click in the 3D window, go to [Simulation Properties], and uncheck [Collision] under [Ground].
If you prefer a cleaner workspace, you can also turn off the [Ground Grid] from the left menu in the 3D window.
Once these settings are adjusted, proceed with simulating the outfit onto the avatar.
Modifying Outfit Details
To achieve optimal performance, 
we need to adjust the mesh type, disable Seam Taping, and modify the Topstitch texture.
First, to convert the entire mesh of the outfit to Quad, 
select all garments using Ctrl + A,  
then go to the [Property Editor] on the right 
panel and set [Geometry] > Mesh Type to [Quad].
Next, disabling unnecessary Seam Taping can further optimize performance.
Select all garments using Ctrl + A, go to the [Property Editor], 
find Selected Line, and set [Seam Taping] to [OFF].
Additionally, if the outfit has Topstitch, check its settings.
If the stitch type is set to OBJ, it increases the mesh count,
which may negatively impact performance.
In this case, switching Topstitch to [Texture] is recommended,  
as it helps reduce the mesh count and improves overall efficiency. 
Now that the outfit is setting, let's move on to the next step.
Rigging
Once the outfit is fitted and all settings are finalized,
open EveryWear by selecting [CONNECT] > [EveryWear] from the top menu.
We will use the [Garment tab] in EveryWear to optimize the 
outfit, apply masking, and proceed with rigging.
Polygon Optimization
First, we will optimize the outfit.
The recommended FBX mesh count is 20,000 polygons or fewer.
To ensure smooth processing, enter 15,000 in the input field next to Garment and proceed with [optimization].
Once optimization is complete, re-simulate the outfit.
However, if the mesh expands after simulation, causing the outfit to clip into the avatar or behave unstably,
it may be best to skip re-simulation.
Evaluate the results and decide whether to keep the simulation based on stability.
Masking
Next, we will remove unnecessary mesh areas through the masking process.
Activate the masking brush by clicking the brush icon next to the Optimize button.
Since AR filter outfits are designed in Thin mode without thickness, we will only apply masking to the Front side of the garment.
Now, use the brush tool to select the mesh areas you want to remove.
If you need to unmask any part during the process, 
switch the Mode to [Subtract] to restore the masked areas.
The masking brush can be used in both the 2D and 3D viewports,
so feel free to work in whichever view is more convenient for you.
Rigging 
Click Apply in the [Rigging tab] to proceed with Auto Rigging.
If weight adjustments are needed, 
use the Weight Brush tools (Add, Subtract, Smooth) to refine the rigging.
If the garment is penetrating the avatar or requires shape adjustments,
utilize the Sculpt Brush tools (Grab, Smooth, Fix Intersection) 
to clean up the surface and refine the shape.
Once all modifications are complete, 
click the [Exit] button to close the Brush window.
UV / Baking
Once rigging is complete, 
navigate to the [Material tab] in the EveryWear window to begin the texture process.
Before proceeding with UV Packing, you need to set the image size.
You can choose from the available options,
but keep in mind that Effect House supports a maximum resolution of 1024x1024. 
For this tutorial, we will use the recommended resolution of 512x512.
After setting the image size and seam size, click the [Pack UVs] button.
Then, adjust the desired settings
and press the Apply button to proceed with UV Packing. 
Once the packing process is complete,
click the [Exit] button to return to the [Material tab].
Next, we will proceed with Texture Baking. 
Before starting, make sure that the 
Ground Collision setting is disabled: 
Right-click in the 3D window - [Simulation Properties] - Disable [Ground Collision]
Select the maps you want to generate, then click the [Apply] button.
For this tutorial, we will use the default settings.
Once the baking process is complete, 
you will be able to see the generated Normal Map and Ambient Occlusion Map.
Once Texture Baking is complete,
the Material List below will automatically generate materials corresponding to the number of UV tiles.
If you want to divide the materials for different parts of the garment in Effect House, 
you can separate and apply them accordingly. 
For this tutorial, 
we will proceed with a single material for the entire garment.
Upload
Once all the work is completed,
click the [Upload] button to open the Export options window. 
Since we are only exporting the garment,
make sure to deselect the avatar.
Also, as thickness is not needed, select the [Thin] option.
Next, select the entire texture and choose [Direct X] from the Graphic Library,
then click [OK] to upload to CONNECT.
Afterward, access CONNECT and download the 
uploaded FBX file.
When you open the downloaded Zip file, you will find the generated FBX file along with the texture map files.
04. Photoshop
In Effect House, the MRAO map is provided as a PBR texture. 
To convert the texture files received from CONNECT into an MRAO map,
we will use Photoshop.
First, open Photoshop,
then select and drag-and-drop the Ambient Occlusion, Metalness, and Roughness maps into Photoshop to load them into separate tabs.
The channel configuration for the MRAO map required by Effect House is as follows:
In this tutorial, we will use the Roughness map 
as the base and add the other maps accordingly.
Select the Roughness tab,
then press Ctrl+A (select all) Ctrl+C (copy). 
Move to the Channel panel, 
select the [Green] channel, and press Ctrl+V (paste). 
Click the AO (Ambient Occlusion) tab,
then press Ctrl+A (select all) Ctrl+C (copy). 
Return to the Roughness tab,
select the [Blue] channel, and press Ctrl+V (paste). 
Select the Metalness tab,
then press Ctrl+A (select all) Ctrl+C (copy). 
Return to the Roughness tab,
select the [Red] channel, and press Ctrl+V (paste).
Once the map creation is complete, 
re-enable the RGB channels to make all channels visible. 
Then, save the file in PNG format.
05. Effect House
We will convert outfits created in CLO and Marvelous Designer into a lens for use on TikTok using Effect House.
First, launch the installed Effect House and type "cloth" in the search bar
to open the Clothing Try-On template.
By default, the template includes a sample Avatar Drive, which is not needed. 
Delete this object from the Hierarchy panel.
Now, let's add lighting.
Click the [Add Object] button in the Hierarchy panel,
then select [Scene Object] > [Environment Light] to set up the lighting.
Next, we will import the outfit and body FBX files.
Click the [+] button in the Assets panel,
then select [Import] > [From Computer]
to bring in BodyRigTemplate.fbx and the FBX file of the outfit created in EveryWear.
Setting Up an Occluder Body
To prevent the body from being visible through the outfit, we 
will set up an occluder body.
Click the [Add Object] button in the Hierarchy panel
and add [AR Tracking] > [Body Avatar Drive].
Once the Body Avatar Drive is created, 
drag the BodyRigTemplate.fbx file from the Assets panel
and drop it under Body Avatar Drive in the Hierarchy panel. 
Select Mesh_Avatar3D under Body Avatar Drive,  
then go to the Inspector panel
and change Material 0 and Material 1 to [Occluder_mat].
Adding the Outfit 
Now, let s add the outfit using the same method we used for the occluder body.
In the Hierarchy panel, 
click the [Add Object] button,
then select [AR Tracking] > [Body Avatar Drive].
Drag and drop the outfit FBX file
under the newly created Body Avatar Drive in the Hierarchy panel. 
In the Preview window on the right, 
check if the outfit is applied correctly.
Applying the Outfit Textures
Let's now apply the textures to the outfit.
In the Assets panel,
click the [+] button,
then select [Import] > [From Computer] to import the Diffuse, MRAO and Opacity maps.
In the Assets panel, click on the [Material 1001] applied to the outfit FBX.
Then, in the Inspector panel, 
activate Texture On for the Albedo, and apply the Diffuse map.
Similarly, check the Opacity box and apply the imported Opacity map.
Activate Texture On for the MRAO map, and apply the imported texture.
If the texture is metallic, adjust the Metallic value to get the desired effect.
You can also adjust the Roughness value.
The default is 0.5, 
but since the textures created in CLO and MD usually have higher roughness,
we ll set it to 0.7.
Now, check if the outfit model and textures are properly applied in Effect House,
then proceed with any additional settings.
Test Performance
If the outfit moves correctly, click the [Test Performance] button at the top.
It's important to check that the AR filter works 
properly on all devices before submitting.
When the Test Performance window appears, 
click [Run Test] and wait for a moment.
Did the result show Passed?
If so, click [Done] and let's proceed with submitting the filter!
Preview on Device
Before submitting the filter, you can preview it.
Click [Preview] in TikTok at the top right, and a QR code will be generated.
Open the TikTok app, 
go to [Profile] > [Add Friend], and scan the QR code.
This will allow you to preview the AR filter you created.
Make sure to check that the AR filter is working correctly!
Create Icon
To upload a thumbnail image, click the [Create Icon] button at the top right.
When the window opens, select [Upload Image] > Select file to upload your own thumbnail image.
Use the slider below the image to adjust its size, 
and once you re satisfied with the settings, click the [Done] button.
Submit
Once all the work is complete, it s time to submit the AR filter.
Click the [Submit] button at the top right.
Set the Effect name and other options, then click the [Next] button.
After reviewing the information you entered, 
click [Submit] to complete the submission.
The submitted AR filter will go through a review process and will be registered.
Approval takes about 1-3 days.
You can check the progress by clicking the avatar icon next to Submit,
which will take you to the Analytics - Manage Effects page in Effect House.
06. Tiktok
Is the filter's status changed to Active?
If so, you're all done!
Click on the filter in the Effect name section to view the QR code.
You can click Share or Save QR code to experience your filter in various environments.
Thank you for participating in the tutorial!
Got a fun idea? Try creating it as an AR filter and enjoy it.
If you have any more questions or need help,
feel free to ask in the CONNECT community board or through the comments!
summary: ```markdown # Everywear To TikTok AR Tutorial (English/한국어) ## 01. Introduction & Purpose Hello, everyone! Have you ever wanted to create your very own AR filter on TikTok featuring a unique outfit? Imagine wearing the outfit you designed and turning it into a one-of-a-kind filter! With EveryWear, the process is much easier and more fun than you might think. To explain it simply, we all know TikTok, right? It's the go-to platform for creating, sharing, and enjoying short-form videos! In this tutorial, we'll walk through the process of transforming garments created in CLO or Marvelous Designer into a TikTok AR filter using EveryWear, Photoshop, and Effect House. If you're new to EveryWear, we recommend checking out the basic tutorials first to get familiar with the fundamentals. We've included useful reference links in the description; be sure to take a look! Now, let's get started! ## 02. Effect House Guidelines To create a TikTok AR filter, we need to use Effect House, TikTok's official AR development program. First, download and install the program from the link below. This tutorial is based on Effect House version 4.11.2. We've also prepared a manual and important guidelines for creating your own AR filters; be sure to check the description for details! When creating your filter in Effect House, make sure to follow these technical requirements. We've also provided a Template Body Mesh file for Effect House, which is essential for designing outfits. You can find the download link in the description, so make sure to grab it! By following these guidelines, you'll be able to create a more stable and stunning AR filter. Now, let's move on to the next step! ## 03. EveryWear ### Downloading the Outfit & Importing the Avatar First, we will create and dress the avatar using CLO. Then, we'll use EveryWear for garment optimization, rigging, and bake map creation. Since EveryWear works the same in both CLO and Marvelous Designer, feel free to use the software you're most comfortable with. The outfit used in this tutorial is provided by CONNECT. Click the link in the card above to access CONNECT. Add the garment to your cart, complete the purchase, and download the file. Import the downloaded file into CLO or Marvelous Designer to begin working. Next, you'll also need to import the BodyRigTemplate.fbx file for Effect House. Simply drag and drop the file into your workspace. When importing, make sure to match the settings shown in the provided reference image. ### Fitting Currently, both the avatar and the outfit are positioned below the Ground. To correct this, we first need to disable the Ground Collision setting. Right-click in the 3D window, go to [Simulation Properties], and uncheck [Collision] under [Ground]. If you prefer a cleaner workspace, you can also turn off the [Ground Grid] from the left menu in the 3D window. Once these settings are adjusted, proceed with simulating the outfit onto the avatar. ### Modifying Outfit Details To achieve optimal performance, we need to adjust the mesh type, disable Seam Taping, and modify the Topstitch texture. First, to convert the entire mesh of the outfit to Quad, select all garments using Ctrl + A, then go to the [Property Editor] on the right panel and set [Geometry] > Mesh Type to [Quad]. Next, disabling unnecessary Seam Taping can further optimize performance. Select all garments using Ctrl + A, go to the [Property Editor], find Selected Line, and set [Seam Taping] to [OFF]. Additionally, if the outfit has Topstitch, check its settings. If the stitch type is set to OBJ, it increases the mesh count, which may negatively impact performance. In this case, switching Topstitch to [Texture] is recommended, as it helps reduce the mesh count and improves overall efficiency. Now that the outfit is set, let's move on to the next step. ### Rigging Once the outfit is fitted and all settings are finalized, open EveryWear by selecting [CONNECT] > [EveryWear] from the top menu. We will use the [Garment tab] in EveryWear to optimize the outfit, apply masking, and proceed with rigging. ### Polygon Optimization First, we will optimize the outfit. The recommended FBX mesh count is 20,000 polygons or fewer. To ensure smooth processing, enter 15,000 in the input field next to Garment and proceed with [optimization]. Once optimization is complete, re-simulate the outfit. However, if the mesh expands after simulation, causing the outfit to clip into the avatar or behave unstably, it may be best to skip re-simulation. Evaluate the results and decide whether to keep the simulation based on stability. ### Masking Next, we will remove unnecessary mesh areas through the masking process. Activate the masking brush by clicking the brush icon next to the Optimize button. Since AR filter outfits are designed in Thin mode without thickness, we will only apply masking to the front side of the garment. Now, use the brush tool to select the mesh areas you want to remove. If you need to unmask any part during the process, switch the Mode to [Subtract] to restore the masked areas. The masking brush can be used in both the 2D and 3D viewports, so feel free to work in whichever view is more convenient for you. ### Rigging Click Apply in the [Rigging tab] to proceed with Auto Rigging. If weight adjustments are needed, use the Weight Brush tools (Add, Subtract, Smooth) to refine the rigging. If the garment is penetrating the avatar or requires shape adjustments, utilize the Sculpt Brush tools (Grab, Smooth, Fix Intersection) to clean up the surface and refine the shape. Once all modifications are complete, click the [Exit] button to close the Brush window. ### UV / Baking Once rigging is complete, navigate to the [Material tab] in the EveryWear window to begin the texture process. Before proceeding with UV Packing, you need to set the image size. You can choose from the available options, but keep in mind that Effect House supports a maximum resolution of 1024x1024. For this tutorial, we will use the recommended resolution of 512x512. After setting the image size and seam size, click the [Pack UVs] button. Then, adjust the desired settings and press the Apply button to proceed with UV Packing. Once the packing process is complete, click the [Exit] button to return to the [Material tab]. Next, we will proceed with Texture Baking. Before starting, make sure that the Ground Collision setting is disabled: Right-click in the 3D window - [Simulation Properties] - Disable [Ground Collision]. Select the maps you want to generate, then click the [Apply] button. For this tutorial, we will use the default settings. Once the baking process is complete, you will be able to see the generated Normal Map and Ambient Occlusion Map. Once Texture Baking is complete, the Material List below will automatically generate materials corresponding to the number of UV tiles. If you want to divide the materials for different parts of the garment in Effect House, you can separate and apply them accordingly. For this tutorial, we will proceed with a single material for the entire garment. ### Upload Once all the work is completed, click the [Upload] button to open the Export options window. Since we are only exporting the garment, make sure to deselect the avatar. Also, as thickness is not needed, select the [Thin] option. Next, select the entire texture and choose [Direct X] from the Graphic Library, then click [OK] to upload to CONNECT. Afterward, access CONNECT and download the uploaded FBX file. When you open the downloaded Zip file, you will find the generated FBX file along with the texture map files. ## 04. Photoshop In Effect House, the MRAO map is provided as a PBR texture. To convert the texture files received from CONNECT into an MRAO map, we will use Photoshop. First, open Photoshop, then select and drag-and-drop the Ambient Occlusion, Metalness, and Roughness maps into Photoshop to load them into separate tabs. The channel configuration for the MRAO map required by Effect House is as follows: In this tutorial, we will use the Roughness map as the base and add the other maps accordingly. Select the Roughness tab, then press Ctrl+A (select all) Ctrl+C (copy). Move to the Channel panel, select the [Green] channel, and press Ctrl+V (paste). Click the AO (Ambient Occlusion) tab, then press Ctrl+A (select all) Ctrl+C (copy). Return to the Roughness tab, select the [Blue] channel, and press Ctrl+V (paste). Select the Metalness tab, then press Ctrl+A (select all) Ctrl+C (copy). Return to the Roughness tab, select the [Red] channel, and press Ctrl+V (paste). Once the map creation is complete, re-enable the RGB channels to make all channels visible. Then, save the file in PNG format. ## 05. Effect House We will convert outfits created in CLO and Marvelous Designer into a lens for use on TikTok using Effect House. First, launch the installed Effect House and type "cloth" in the search bar to open the Clothing Try-On template. By default, the template includes a sample Avatar Drive, which is not needed. Delete this object from the Hierarchy panel. ### Adding Lighting Now, let's add lighting. Click the [Add Object] button in the Hierarchy panel

summary: ```markdown # Clo 2025.0 Features Highlights ## Introduction Hey everyone, Clo 2025.0 is all about making your design process magical. Harnessing AI allows you to focus on the creative while we handle the mundane. Let's dive into our biggest updates. ## Key Features ### Beta AI Pose Generator Our beta AI pose generator will automatically create dynamic poses for you, making the time-consuming work of creating poses obsolete. You'll be able to use either Clo's updated prompt system to generate poses closer to your ideas or bring in your own images. ### Saving and Applying Poses Once your pose is created, you can easily save it and then apply that pose to any of your Clo projects. ### Enhanced Pattern Drafter Our pattern drafter takes parametric design a step further. Now, you can create a range of shirt styles using our patented measurement technique. Simply type in your measurements, and Clo will guide you on where and how that measurement will adjust a pattern. ### AI Pattern Drafter Using our beta AI pattern drafter, you can start with just a sketch. Either have Clo generate a sketch from our prompt tools or drop in one of your own sketches, and Clo will generate the measurements for you. You can continue to adjust and design further. Once ready, simply select create, and Clo will arrange and sew your designs just like magic. ## Animation Editor Updates Our animation editor UI has been updated to now include key frames. These key frames allow for quick editing within animation, along with a range of editing options to choose from, providing more precision and control. You'll now have the ability to activate or deactivate various assets within Clo, ranging from gravity to colorway, making it possible to create exciting and powerful new animations. ## 3D Window Enhancements You will now be able to see fur within your 3D window, allowing you to make more decisions without needing to go into your render window. Simply switch to fur strand type within our material section, and you'll be able to see your fur immediately. This will also show up in the render window. ## Print Layout Upgrade Print layout has received a huge upgrade, along with your production workflows. With our new texture nesting feature, we can now read and follow the placement of your textures within the 3D window and ensure the placement is mirrored when nesting the pattern. Simply select the pattern matching, and depending on the type of texture application, choose either texture, print, or lock. ## Avatar Improvements ### AI Studio Enhancements AI Studio has been upgraded to include a background option while also improving the overall output of images. Once opened, you can adjust either the avatar or the background. You can also utilize our prompts by using keywords or writing in your ideas to create the images. ### Image Upload and Environment Creation If you have an image already, you can upload it into our studio. Our studio will rework the image to create the desired environment for your garment. ### IK Joint Mapping We have added IK joint mapping for FBX avatars, allowing for more compatibility with external avatars. The process is straightforward: select the point in the 3D window that matches with the one in the avatar editor, or let Clo figure it out with our auto-match feature. Once applied, any pose in Clo can be applied to this avatar. ### Flip Pose Feature Flip pose is a great new simple addition to our avatar features, allowing you to flip any pose you have within the 3D window. ### Avatar Editor Improvements Our avatar editor is continuously improving. The latest update enhances hip and breast control. You can now control the shaping of the hips, deciding how they should dip in or out of the body, and also control the bottom of the avatar, whether it should be round or flat. For breasts, you have the option of adding cup sizes, either using your own or our default cup sizes. ## 3D Window Update Our UV editor has been integrated into the materials and UV toolbar. You can now export the back or side of your textures within the UV editor for better compatibility outside of Clo. ## Rendering Updates We have added the option to choose your colorways within the 3D snapshot. This works for both single snapshots and multi-snapshots. You can select all colorways or just specific ones, allowing you to quickly export multiple colorways of your project all at once. ### Depth of Field Control You now have more control within your render window and custom views. You can control the depth of field through each custom view by using the left click to find your focus point, and Clo will automatically apply it to the custom view. ## Trim Improvements Attaching trims within Clo is easier than ever. Utilizing the tack tool for trims, you can create multiple attachment points on a single trim by selecting the tack tool, clicking on the trim, and then the pattern piece you want the trim to attach to. ## Simulation Update We have added an option to our 3D selection tool called advanced pinching, which allows control over what and how much you are selecting. You can use sliders to control the amount selected and checkboxes to decide which pattern should be affected. ## UI Enhancements Now, when bringing in a project file, you can choose whether to open the toggle menu within that project file or use the default toggle menu. We have also added a new library window within Clo, making it easier to use. You can transfer all previous library folders to the new library and rename the folders as needed. ## Material Updates More user-friendly tools have been added into Clo's colorways. Using the shortcut key "O," you can open the colorway. Within the object browser, you can cycle through the color chips and see the different colorways. Once open, you can edit the front, back, or side of the fabric within the colorway editor. ## Grading and DXF Enhancements We have made annotations within Clo even easier to edit. You can now change color, size, edit the text, and rotate the annotation all within the 2D window. ## 2D CAD Improvements Our smooth curve tool has become more powerful than ever. With the ability to use the tool in the original method, we have included a new method involving curve points, giving you more control over editing your curves and ensuring that only part of the pattern will be adjusted. ## Conclusion There are many more features that we have worked on that are included within this release, elevating your editing capabilities to a whole new level. Here are just a few more exciting features to mention. Thanks for watching! Stay tuned for our upcoming deep dives where you'll learn all about the new features. If you have any questions, drop them in the comments section below. Happy creating! ```

summary: # Akira Pants Construction by @Sam_Fromonline ## Introduction What's up, losers? We are back! We are virtually sewing on the laptop, of course, and today we are entering part one of constructing one of, if not the hardest, outfits in anime. Everyone knows Kaneda's iconic red and signal orange biker suit from *Akira*. It's inspired so much in pop culture and fashion for decades, so I want to give it the recognition it deserves. ## Pattern Preparation We’re going to start the process by importing my basic button-fly pant block pattern to work off of. I decided to go with a heavy nylon canvas and dragged that over to all my selected pattern pieces. I did use the Photoshop eyedropper tool to find the exact color of this neon orange for his pants according to my reference images. So don’t come for me if you think it’s supposed to be red or something! ## Pocket Design I’m drawing in these patch pockets using internal lines, loosely based on the reference image with the rounded corners, and cutting off the top corner for much easier hand access. Then, I duplicated the shape as its own pattern piece and sewed both of them down to the front of the pants on both sides. Boom! We have two perfect pockets. Honestly, I really like this pocket shape; this is something I’m definitely going to explore in the future. ## Knee Pad Placement I made the 3D visualization transparent so I could find exactly where the knees hit on the pants, allowing me to place the knee pads. I did take some liberties with these and made them a little bigger than the reference. I wanted to express this more as a double knee than an actual knee cushion like you see in the anime—just something a bit more realistic. ## Triple Knee Concept By double knee, I actually meant triple knee. I cut out these extra pieces and reinforced them with another layer of fabric, which created more of a traditional moto pant look and shape, making three total layers. ## Back Pocket Addition Finally, for the last step, I’m borrowing the shape of the knee pads to use as back pockets. The original reference didn’t have these, but it looked too plain to me without them. I like to share shapes across the whole design. I copied the shape, cloned it as a pattern piece, sewed them on, and then added the top stitching to complete the look. ## Conclusion Let me know what you guys think of these finished Kaneda pants! Follow for part two, where I'm going to tackle his iconic jacket. I’ll see you guys in the next one. Bye!

summary: ```markdown # Texturing A Dreamy Dress In Clo 2024.2 🧚‍♀️ ## Introduction Let me guide you through the texturing of this dreamy dress in Clo 2024.2 and showcase some of the exciting new features. ## Color Harmonization To harmonize the colors, I used the new color switch tool in the image editor. I selected how many colors to extract and modified them individually. Once I had the right palette, I autogenerated the normal map and moved to the next fabric. ## Seamless Texturing For this fabric, I aimed to retain the landscape's art style but reduce details. To achieve this, I generated a seamless texture from one image segment. When satisfied with the selection, I proceeded to the knit. ## Knitted Details To blend the knitted details with the garment, I utilized a new yarn variance feature. This feature allowed me to add imperfections for a natural look and feel. ## Conclusion Which one of these great features is your favorite? ```

summary: ```markdown # Design Process By Atelier Bantu Giant ## Introduction This is how you get your clothing designs right without endless samples and back and forth with your suppliers. The first step in creating any garment is having a clear vision. ## Inspiration Whatever the idea—sketch or image reference—for example, today's inspiration comes from this beautiful AC Studio garment with a strong concept. ## Design Software: CLO 3D We can move forward using CLO 3D for my design process. Why CLO 3D? It allows us to visualize garments in real time with accurate fabric simulation and precise detailing. ### Benefits of CLO 3D This means you can see how the fabric drapes, how the stitching looks, and even how the garment fits on a model—all before a single physical sample is made. ## Attention to Detail I also ensure every detail is included to communicate clearly with the manufacturers, from fabric choices and measurements to construction techniques. This really helps the production process and ensures that we achieve the perfect result from start to finish, while also saving time and costs. ## Collaboration I go by Osara, and if you're looking for a 3D apparel designer specializing in pattern making and tech packaging, let's talk. ```

summary: # How To Create Knitwear In Clo! Skill-Up Webinar ## Introduction In this webinar, we will explore how to create a beautiful knitwear outfit, including a skirt and a beret, using Clo. Our focus will be on the knitwear part, incorporating patches and lighting effects. ## Overview of the Outfit - **Created by**: Celia from the Spanish team. - **Components**: Knitwear outfit with a skirt and a beret. - **Focus Areas**: - Knitwear texture. - Incorporating patches. - Adding lighting effects. ## Setting Up the Environment To begin, we need to turn on the render settings as some elements, such as lights and certain materials, are not visible in the 3D viewer but appear in the render. The realistic knitwear function is quite resource-intensive, so be prepared for potential slowdowns on your computer. ### Opening the Project File - **File to open**: `skillup knitwear start`. - **Library Management**: Use the letter "Y" on your keyboard to open and close the library. ## Understanding the Knitwear Function The knitwear function, introduced in the 2024 version of Clo, allows for realistic rendering of knit materials. ### Key Features of the Knitwear Function 1. **Material Selection**: Change the material type through the property editor. - Available options: Shiny fabric, fur, knitwear. 2. **3D Mesh Structure**: Each loop in the knitwear becomes its own 3D mesh, making the rendering process computationally heavy. ## Working with Knitwear Materials ### Changing the Material Type 1. Select the desired knitwear material (e.g., 2x2 rib). 2. Ensure you select the appropriate preset for the type of knit. ### Adjusting Yarn Thickness and Gauge - **Yarn Thickness**: Adjust from 0.5 mm to 5 mm to see the effect on the knit. - **Gauge**: Measured per inch, it controls the tightness of the loops, ranging from 1 to 16. ### Additional Material Settings - **Knit Direction**: Change the angle of the knit (default is 0°). - **Ply Amount**: Adjust the number of yarns used (1 to 6 ply). - **Color Selection**: Choose yarn colors, and apply randomization for a more realistic effect. ## Advanced Features ### Yarn Variance - Adjusts the texture of the yarn, providing either a regular or irregular appearance. - Change the frequency and magnitude of the variance for desired effects. ### Pilling - Pilling occurs when short fibers create small balls on the knit surface. - Activate the pilling option to simulate this effect, adjusting thickness and frequency as needed. ### Generate Seams - Activate this option to create visible seam lines on your garment for realism. ### Importing Images as Textures - Drag and drop images into the base color map to create unique knitwear patterns. ## Adding Patches ### Dog Patch Application 1. Locate the dog patch in the training folder and apply it to the front pattern. 2. Adjust the size of the patch using the graphic transformation tool. 3. Connect texture maps (normal, displacement, opacity, roughness) to the corresponding channels. ### Tree Patches 1. Apply similar steps as the dog patch, ensuring to use the appropriate texture maps for the tree patches. 2. Change the material type from fabric to fur as needed. ## Creating Decorative Elements ### Top Stitch for Cables 1. Create a new top stitch for the cable lights, adjusting the offset to align with the internal line of the garment. 2. Set the material type to fur for a fluffy effect. ### Adding Lights 1. Use the trim tab to access the light trim and apply it to the patches. 2. Glue the lights onto the patches and change their material type to light. ## Conclusion In this webinar, we've covered: - Creating a knitwear outfit in Clo. - Applying textures and materials effectively. - Utilizing advanced features like yarn variance and image importing. ### Next Steps Feel free to leave any questions in the chat! We will address them shortly. Thank you for participating, and we look forward to seeing you in our next session in Q1 2025. Happy holidays!
