transcript:
Introduction
Hello, everyone! 
Welcome to the EveryWear 2024.2 New Features Tutorial. 
EveryWear provides an easy optimization function 
for garments made in CLO and Marvelous Designer,  
making them ready for digital spaces like 
games, the metaverse, and entertainment.
You can find the EveryWear Basics Tutorial at the link above. 
In this tutorial, we will introduce the new features of EveryWear 2024.2
UI Update
The position of EveryWear has been updated. 
The icon that was previously located in  
the upper right corner has now moved 
under the CONNECT tab in the Main Menu.
Show Wireframe
In the garment rendering modes on the left side of the 3D window,  
a new option, 'Show Wireframe,' has been added 
under the Garment Rendering Options. 
This makes it easier to understand the mesh structure 
at a glance and work more efficiently.
Auto Rigging Quality Upgrade
The accuracy of Auto Rigging has been remarkably  
improved with the release of CLO 2024.2.
You can now achieve higher-quality rigging  
results, especially in areas that typically require more adjustments,  
such as the armpits and areas around the crotch.
Thickness
A Thickness feature has been added 
to allow for realistic garment thickness representation.
To apply thickness, select the pattern and go to the Property Editor on the right. 
Under Geometry, edit the properties by following these steps.
In the ‘Add’l Thickness - Rendering (mm)’ section,  
set the preferred thickness value for your pattern. 
Please make sure that the ‘Thickness’  
is only visible when Thick Textured Surface (Alt+1) is selected in the 3D window.
In the ‘Extrusion Direction', you can select your preferred direction for the ‘Thickness.’ 
Choosing ‘Both’ applies thickness to both the front and back of the pattern.
 ‘Forward’ applies thickness to the front side, 
while ‘Backward’ applies it to the inner side. 
In the ‘Face Visible Option’, specify which 
side of the face you want to display based  
on the normal direction: 
‘Front Face’ will show the front side,
‘Back Face’ will show the reverse side, 
and ‘Seam Face’ will reveal  the side that overlaps with the seam line.
Side Geometry
You can adjust the ‘Curvature’ to control how rounded the edges are. 
The closer the value is  
to 100, the rounder the edges will look, 
while a value closer to 0 will make the edges sharper.
The ‘Resolution’ lets you set the number of divisions for the side mesh.  
The default value is 6, but you can set it between 0 and 10. 
Setting it to 0 will remove the entire side mesh. 
A minimum Resolution value of 2 is required for the ‘Curvature’ to take effect. 
Additionally, you can use the Edit Pattern tool to apply different resolution values to  
individual segments by clicking each line segment.
Tip: Since the default Resolution value for all patterns is set to 6,
 we recommend either  
lowering it below 6 or removing the thickness 
by setting it to 0 if you want to optimize the mesh.
Mask Brush 
The ‘Mask Brush’ feature lets you mask specific areas of the garment,  
allowing you to retain only the desired parts and export optimized garment data.
To use the tool, click the ‘Brush’ icon next to ‘Polygon Optimization’ 
to enter the Mask Brush tab. 
The Front and Back tabs refer to the 2D pattern view, though both sides can  
be masked in the 3D window. 
Choose a Mode to add or subtract masked areas.
Adjust the Size to control the brush diameter.   
Selecting Clear All Masks removes entire masks applied to the Front or Back views.
Pressing ‘Reset’ will return the Mode and Size to their defaults,  
while ‘Exit’ will close the Mask Brush window and return to the EveryWear interface.
Weight Brush : Smooth (Multiple Joints)
The Smooth Weight Brush for Multiple Joints has been added,
 making joint weight adjustment easier than before.
This Smooth Brush works across all joints,  
smoothing each vertex's joint weight in coordination with  
surrounding vertex joint weights without needing joint selection. 
This feature works like selecting all joints in the Single Brush, allowing for smooth  
adjustments of joint weights at each vertex while maintaining a total joint weight of 1.
To use the brush, select the Brush tool, then in Weight Mode,  
choose Smooth (Multiple Joints) under Blend Mode. 
Adjust the Strength, Size,  
Focal, and Depth values as desired, then click and drag to apply to the model.
Sculpt Brush : Fix Intersection
This feature is particularly useful when mesh intersections occur between  
the avatar and the garment, or between different garments,  
as it can be challenging to resolve these issues with conventional brushes.
To apply, select the Brush Tool, then in Sculpt Mode,  
choose Blend Mode - Fix Intersection. 
Adjust the Strength, Size, Focal,  
and Depth values as desired, then click and drag to apply to the model.
This feature automatically resolves intersecting areas  
between the garment and avatar, or between different garments.
UV Packing Upgrade
The ‘Fidelity’ and ‘Advanced Placement’ options have been added to the ‘UV Packing.’ 
Under the Material tab, click the ‘Pack UVs’ button to enter the UV Packing tab. 
Fidelity sets UV accuracy on a scale from 1 to 5. 
Setting it to 1 will simplify the UV pieces, 
resulting in faster placement but potentially lower packing quality. 
On the other hand,
setting it to 5 will arrange the pieces in their original shapes,  
yielding higher packing quality but with a slower processing time.
Enabling the ‘Advanced Placement’ applies a variety of layout methods. 
Minimizing empty
spaces for more precise arrangement. 
However, this may increase the packing time.
Upload - Thin/Thick
The Thin / Thick options have been added to the Export options window. 
By default, all patterns have a Resolution value of 6 applied. 
If you don’t want to add thickness to the garment, select Thin in  
the export options before exporting. 
However, if you want to apply thickness  
values or have specifically added thickness to the garment, 
choose the Thick option when exporting.
summary: ```markdown # Discover The New Everywear Features In Clo 2024.2 ## Introduction Hello, everyone! Welcome to the EveryWear 2024.2 New Features Tutorial. EveryWear provides an easy optimization function for garments made in CLO and Marvelous Designer, making them ready for digital spaces like games, the metaverse, and entertainment. You can find the EveryWear Basics Tutorial at the link above. In this tutorial, we will introduce the new features of EveryWear 2024.2. ## UI Update The position of EveryWear has been updated. The icon that was previously located in the upper right corner has now moved under the CONNECT tab in the Main Menu. ## Show Wireframe In the garment rendering modes on the left side of the 3D window, a new option, 'Show Wireframe,' has been added under the Garment Rendering Options. This makes it easier to understand the mesh structure at a glance and work more efficiently. ## Auto Rigging Quality Upgrade The accuracy of Auto Rigging has been remarkably improved with the release of CLO 2024.2. You can now achieve higher-quality rigging results, especially in areas that typically require more adjustments, such as the armpits and areas around the crotch. ## Thickness A Thickness feature has been added to allow for realistic garment thickness representation. To apply thickness, select the pattern and go to the Property Editor on the right. Under Geometry, edit the properties by following these steps: 1. In the ‘Add’l Thickness - Rendering (mm)’ section, set the preferred thickness value for your pattern. 2. Please make sure that the ‘Thickness’ is only visible when Thick Textured Surface (Alt+1) is selected in the 3D window. 3. In the ‘Extrusion Direction', you can select your preferred direction for the ‘Thickness.’ - Choosing ‘Both’ applies thickness to both the front and back of the pattern. - ‘Forward’ applies thickness to the front side, while ‘Backward’ applies it to the inner side. 4. In the ‘Face Visible Option’, specify which side of the face you want to display based on the normal direction: - ‘Front Face’ will show the front side, - ‘Back Face’ will show the reverse side, - ‘Seam Face’ will reveal the side that overlaps with the seam line. ## Side Geometry You can adjust the ‘Curvature’ to control how rounded the edges are. The closer the value is to 100, the rounder the edges will look, while a value closer to 0 will make the edges sharper. The ‘Resolution’ lets you set the number of divisions for the side mesh. The default value is 6, but you can set it between 0 and 10. Setting it to 0 will remove the entire side mesh. A minimum Resolution value of 2 is required for the ‘Curvature’ to take effect. Additionally, you can use the Edit Pattern tool to apply different resolution values to individual segments by clicking each line segment. **Tip:** Since the default Resolution value for all patterns is set to 6, we recommend either lowering it below 6 or removing the thickness by setting it to 0 if you want to optimize the mesh. ## Mask Brush The ‘Mask Brush’ feature lets you mask specific areas of the garment, allowing you to retain only the desired parts and export optimized garment data. To use the tool, click the ‘Brush’ icon next to ‘Polygon Optimization’ to enter the Mask Brush tab. The Front and Back tabs refer to the 2D pattern view, though both sides can be masked in the 3D window. Choose a Mode to add or subtract masked areas. Adjust the Size to control the brush diameter. - Selecting Clear All Masks removes entire masks applied to the Front or Back views. - Pressing ‘Reset’ will return the Mode and Size to their defaults, while ‘Exit’ will close the Mask Brush window and return to the EveryWear interface. ## Weight Brush: Smooth (Multiple Joints) The Smooth Weight Brush for Multiple Joints has been added, making joint weight adjustment easier than before. This Smooth Brush works across all joints, smoothing each vertex's joint weight in coordination with surrounding vertex joint weights without needing joint selection. This feature works like selecting all joints in the Single Brush, allowing for smooth adjustments of joint weights at each vertex while maintaining a total joint weight of 1. To use the brush, select the Brush tool, then in Weight Mode, choose Smooth (Multiple Joints) under Blend Mode. Adjust the Strength, Size, Focal, and Depth values as desired, then click and drag to apply to the model. ## Sculpt Brush: Fix Intersection This feature is particularly useful when mesh intersections occur between the avatar and the garment, or between different garments, as it can be challenging to resolve these issues with conventional brushes. To apply, select the Brush Tool, then in Sculpt Mode, choose Blend Mode - Fix Intersection. Adjust the Strength, Size, Focal, and Depth values as desired, then click and drag to apply to the model. This feature automatically resolves intersecting areas between the garment and avatar, or between different garments. ## UV Packing Upgrade The ‘Fidelity’ and ‘Advanced Placement’ options have been added to the ‘UV Packing.’ Under the Material tab, click the ‘Pack UVs’ button to enter the UV Packing tab. - Fidelity sets UV accuracy on a scale from 1 to 5. Setting it to 1 will simplify the UV pieces, resulting in faster placement but potentially lower packing quality. - On the other hand, setting it to 5 will arrange the pieces in their original shapes, yielding higher packing quality but with a slower processing time. Enabling the ‘Advanced Placement’ applies a variety of layout methods, minimizing empty spaces for more precise arrangement. However, this may increase the packing time. ## Upload - Thin/Thick The Thin / Thick options have been added to the Export options window. By default, all patterns have a Resolution value of 6 applied. If you don’t want to add thickness to the garment, select Thin in the export options before exporting. However, if you want to apply thickness values or have specifically added thickness to the garment, choose the Thick option when exporting. ```

It's super exciting, so let's dive on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Overview of Updates Here I have my screen, and as you can see, I have this cute little CL emblem as my collar button. I brought it in as an OBJ trim. The update here, especially for grading, is that now we can grade OBJ trims and buttons, along with all of your trims and everything. ## Gluing Your Trim So, let's see how we do that. First off, you have to make sure you glue your trim. There are a few ways to know if your trim is glued. If you select your trim, you can see that the glue bottle is blue. Additionally, you'll notice that there is a mark on your pattern piece, which is a little plus sign. This is new, and the reason we have this mark is so you can grade it. That's another way to know if something is glued. If something's not glued, the glue bottle won't be blue; it won't be filled, and it won't indicate that it's gluing. ### Ungluing Your Trim You can unglue by clicking this option, and then it will turn it off. Alternatively, you can right-click and select "unglue." Now it's unglued. If I zoom out, you won't see that little plus sign on this side. So this one is glued, while this one is no longer glued, as evidenced by the absence of the plus sign or any mark indicating it's glued. ## Gluing Technique Don't worry; you can easily glue something. There is a trick: always make sure that you click the right point on your trim. For this one, since I want to ensure that the center of my trim aligns with the center of the C, that's my gluing spot. I’m going to put my cursor right in the center, which will be my gluing spot. I’ll then go to my little glue bottle to turn this on and activate it. After placing it right here, you’ll see the little plus sign indicating it’s glued. You can always click again and reglue it if needed. If I want to reglue it anywhere, I could do that as well. ### Adjusting the Glue Placement If there's anything wrong with the exact placement or if you need adjustments, you can always rotate and adjust it. It's all good! ## Adding Grading Now that it's glued and set, I can add my grading. You can do this easily by going to your Edit Grading tool in your grading section in the 2D window. Make sure your pattern pieces already have grading assigned. I’ve actually already graded most of my patterns and assigned grading to them. Now all I have to do is select my little marker and, using my arrow keys on my keyboard, I can add in that grading. You can also input it through measurements if you prefer. ### Finalizing Grading I’ll just go over here and add in the grading as well, and voila! That’s it! Isn’t that great? We can do the exact same steps for our buttons. You can select multiple buttons at once by holding down the Shift key and selecting them. After that, right-click and paste. You can paste X and Y, just X, or just Y. summary: # Easily Change Your Pattern Outline Length in Clo | Clo Feature Deep Dive ## Introduction Hi, my name is Phoebe, and I have a great update to change length to show you all. So, let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Editing Patterns Here I have my patterns, and I'm ready to start editing them. Now, instead of just being able to select one segment or, if this was cut up, select two segments, I can do something really cool. ### Selecting Multiple Pattern Outlines Now, I can select pattern outlines from different patterns. For example, I can select this pattern outline and this pattern outline, right-click, and change the length. I can then type in what I want my new length to be. So, I want it to be 12.5. ### Adjusting Directions Of course, I can adjust directions, but since this is a half-symmetrical pattern, the start is going to be the only direction that this pattern will work in. If I go to both, you'll see that this no longer goes to either side, but you'll see that this pattern will adjust because it doesn't have the half-symmetry applied to it. I could go to end, and again this won't apply here, but it will apply here. Then I could go to start, and then it will apply to both, which is good. Great! I can then hit okay, and I'll see my update. ## Linking Internal Lines Now, you might say, "Oh, now I have to adjust and edit the internal lines." But if you want to avoid that, there’s this really great feature that we added to Clo a while ago: link to pattern outline. ### Using the Transform Pattern Tool We got to it by using our transform pattern tool. You select the internal line, then just right-click, and you can link to pattern outline. I'll select the pattern outline I want to link to. I’ll do the same for this one; I’ll right-click and link to pattern outline, selecting the pattern outline I want to link it to. Then I can go to my edit pattern tool, select those two pattern outlines from different pattern pieces, and right-click to change length. I'm going to type in 12 again, hit okay, and the internal lines will move with it too. ### Benefits of the Feature This feature is really cool and makes adjusting and editing lines so much easier and better. ## Caveats to Consider There are some things to know and some caveats to this feature that I want to make sure you’re all aware of. One of them is this: here I selected my side seams, and if I right-click and change length, you’ll see that these arrows are going in the same direction. This means adjusting this will work really well. ### Direction of Arrows If I select these two side seams, right-click, and hit change length, you're going to see that these arrows are kind of going in the same direction. However, I would actually have wanted this arrow to be pointing in this way and this arrow to stay in the direction it is. As of now, there isn’t any way to change the direction of a certain line, but there probably will be in the future. If this does happen, just know that you can still go to that great original right-click, change length, adjust your length, and change the direction. ## Matching Lines For example, I could go to end and do 5.25, hit okay, and then don’t forget we have that great feature within Clo where you could select both lines, right-click, match up, and match to measurement. This will allow you to match to the longest or the shortest and adjust it in either way you want. ### Additional Editing Options There are still a lot of ways to easily make sure that both lines are matched up or adjust lines. You can also right-click and link your lines together, then adjust them as needed. When you’re done, you can right-click and unlink the lines. There's a lot of options we have in which you can edit two lines together or apart. The change length feature is just our most recent update to it all. ## Conclusion I think that’s everything! Thank you so much for watching. If you have any questions, check out the comment section below. Also, don't forget to like and subscribe. There’s so much information out there that you can learn and gain, so check out all the videos. Thanks again so much for watching!

summary: ```markdown # How To Use Color Switch | Clo Feature Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey all you clovers! It's Phoebe, and I have a really cool update for you regarding colors and texture switching. Let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Overview of the Project Here, I have three corsets, and we're going to do two things to two of them. The first one is going to stick with being the original. The second one will switch out with a color, and the third one will also switch out with a color. ## Property Editor Options In my property editor below, you can see my base color map. There’s a new recolor option that includes: - **Recolor** - **Desaturate** - **Switch** We all know what desaturate does, but switch is the new feature. Some of you might be familiar with it if you've watched the multitexture editor videos, but we're going to go through those now. ## Using Desaturate For the first corset, we're going to use desaturate. I’ll select desaturate, go to color, and switch it out with this green. After hitting apply and close, you'll notice that with desaturate, we can increase the intensity and play around with the brightness. However, it changes the whole art and desaturates everything, meaning you lose the true texture, print, and repeat. This is why we introduced the switch option in the recolor settings. ## Using Switch Now, for the third corset, we will use the same green color but instead of desaturate, we’ll use switch. After applying and closing, you will see that it actually took one of the colors in this print and switched it out with the green. ### Summary of Color Options To summarize, you have three options for changing out colors: 1. Add the color on top. 2. Desaturate the color. 3. Switch out a color. ## Multi-Texture Editor A few other facts about the color switch: it works exactly the same as our color switch in the multi-texture editor. For those of you who might be wondering, "Phoebe, what's a multi-texture editor?" Well, it's an excellent feature we’ve had for quite some time in Clo. If I go to my base color map and click on the dots, I can open up my texture editor. Here, I can select my fabric. ### Color Switching in Multi-Texture Editor Currently, the color switch is checked on with just one color. If you have a multi-colored print like I do, it would be great to have two, three, or even four colors. I will increase this to three colors. Now, I’m going to select this color and switch it out with that green, close it, select the dark one, switch it out with that ruby kind of green, and finally, select this one to go with a darker green. After applying and closing, you’ll see that I have switched out my three colors to more of a green, staying true to the original artwork while achieving the desired color change. ## Conclusion This is how the color switch works. It’s exactly the same in the multi-texture editor, but you’ll have to go into that editor to add extra colors if you want to switch out more than just one. As you can see, the switch feature is incredibly helpful when you want to maintain the color and texture closer to the original while simply flipping out a color. I think it's really exciting, and I’m happy we have it because it will make all of your color changes so much cooler and fun! Thank you so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section below. If you want to learn more, check out our channel, like, and subscribe for updates on new videos. Keep on having fun in Clo! ```
